_readme: Curated opening hours for POIs OpenStreetMap doesn't carry.
Every entry records where the hours came from and when they were checked, so a
stale or wrong entry can be traced and re-verified rather than argued about.
Applied to public/data/skymap-data.json by scripts/apply-hours-overlay.mjs, and
kept separate from the extraction so `npm run data:osm` can't silently drop it.
- First-party sources only: the business's own site, or its own listing on its
chain's locator. Another company's curated hours database is theirs, not ours.
- If a page states two schedules that disagree, do not pick one. Leave it out
and note it in `skipped` below. A confidently wrong 'Open' is worse than a
blank line: it sends someone to a locked door.
- `00:00-00:00` in schema.org means CLOSED that day. Omit the day; never
translate it as open all day.
- Values are OSM opening_hours syntax, the same grammar src/opening-hours.ts
Contribute these upstream to OSM too — then the extraction picks them up and
this file shrinks instead of growing.

urban-works-skyway-operations-summary.whyBarred: Its own footer reads 'COMPILED BY URBAN WORKS, INC. (c) 2021 Urban Works, Inc.' Urban Works operates skywayaccess.com, whose terms forbid 'Unauthorized reproduction, publication, distribution, or exhibition of any information or materials supplied by our Services' and accessing them 'through any means other than through the interface which is provided by Urban Works'. Being re-hosted by the Downtown Council does not change who compiled it or who holds the copyright — taking it from there is the same breach through a different door.
urban-works-skyway-operations-summary.alsoStale: Dated Thursday, September 9, 2021, and self-reported by buildings, so even if licensed it would predate the post-pandemic changes the City's 2025 committee record describes. Its entry for 100 Washington Square (open daily) already disagrees with that building's current landlord handbook (closed weekends).
urban-works-skyway-operations-summary.action: Not used. Downloaded copies and extracted text were deleted. If Joey wants this data, the route is to license it from Urban Works or ask the Downtown Council for permission — it would close most of the remaining building gap in one step, so it may well be worth asking.
